headline: All segments grow as Baxter lifts full-year outlook
summary_short: Baxter's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 5% y/y to $2.96B on growth in every segment, with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.24 (up from $0.18) aided by a $0.11/share tariff refund. The company raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.95-$2.15 from $1.85-$2.05.
summary_long: Revenue grew 5% y/y to $2.96B (also +5% organic) with growth in every segment: Medical Products & Therapies +7%/+5% organic to $2.076B, led by Drug Compounding and IV Solutions, partly offset by the ongoing Novum IQ LVP shipment hold; Healthcare Systems & Technologies +4% to $801M on Patient Support Systems demand. Operating income rose 14% to $217M as gross margin held near flat (34.9% vs 35.3%). GAAP diluted EPS of $0.24 (vs $0.18) and adjusted EPS of $0.54 (flat y/y) included an $0.11/share tariff refund offsetting higher-cost inventory roll-through and an SG&A-to-COGS reclassification. Baxter raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $1.95-$2.15 (from $1.85-$2.05) and sales-growth guidance to 3%-4% (from flat-to-1%). Cash rose to $2.15B; free cash flow was $181M.

The release explicitly raises FY2026 guidance with stated prior ranges (reported sales growth to 3%-4% from flat-to-1%; organic sales growth to 2%-3% from approximately flat; adjusted diluted EPS to $1.95-$2.15 from $1.85-$2.05) -- this qualifies as a 'raised' move with prior range disclosed, but it was captured narratively in summary_long above rather than written into the event shard's structured guidance[] array because no sanctioned script exists for that write (scripts/ has no guidance-apply equivalent to apply-extended-metrics.mjs) and the tooling rule forbids ad-hoc node -e shard edits -- flagging as a tooling gap rather than fabricating the write. drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based across all segments and divisions in both the U.S. and internationally; Medical Products & Therapies rose on Drug Compounding, IV Solutions, and Advanced Surgery demand, partly offset by the Novum IQ LVP shipment/installation hold and lower Injectables sales.

13.6% y/y growth against 5.3% revenue growth reflects operating leverage from the sales increase, with special items (intangible amortization, business optimization, separation costs) similar in scale to a year ago.
Tracks the net-income improvement to $126M from $91M a year ago, driven by higher operating income and a lower discontinued-operations loss.
Flat y/y as an $0.11/share IEEPA tariff refund offset the roll-through of higher-cost inventory produced in late 2025 and an unfavorable SG&A-to-cost-of-sales reclassification versus the prior year.
Company cited operating performance plus the unbudgeted tariff refund as the reason results beat expectations, and raised its full-year 2026 outlook for sales growth and adjusted EPS.
